title: ORFE Upcoming Events (newsletter variant)
description: Schema for events-newsletter.json: the subset of the feed falling inside the next newsletter edition's coverage window. A strict superset of events.schema.json -- it additionally requires title provenance and the edition stamp. Self-contained rather than $ref'ing the base schema, because tools/validate_json.py builds a bare Draft7Validator with no RefResolver.

guid.description: Stable unique identifier from ICS UID (e.g., ps_events:11876:delta:0).

startTime.description: Event start in target timezone formatted as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss (no timezone suffix).

endTime.description: Event end in target timezone formatted as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss (no timezone suffix).

urlRef.description: URL to the event detail page.

id.description: Reserved for future canonical location id (may be empty).

series.description: Joined categories string (comma-separated) from ICS CATEGORIES.

speaker.description: ICS SUMMARY field with commas/semicolons escaped (\, \;).

content.description: Event abstract/description. Derived from ICS DESCRIPTION unless content enrichment is enabled. Newlines may be normalized depending on configuration.

title.description: Title populated via enrichment (subtitle), fallback from speaker/template, or a series-derived last resort; never empty.

cancelled.description: Placeholder field for cancellation status (currently empty string).

bannerImage.description: Placeholder field for hero image URL (currently empty string).

rawEventDetails.description: Optional inner HTML fragment from .events-detail-main of the event page.

titleSource.description: Where the title came from. 'enriched' (scraped subtitle) and 'ics' (supplied by the feed) are real titles; the 'fallback-*' values are synthesized by this pipeline.

titleIsPlaceholder.description: True when the title was synthesized because no real one was available yet. Editors should treat these as unpublishable.

newsletterEdition.description: Stable id of the edition this variant was built for: the week-anchor Monday, even when publication is shifted (e.g. Labor Day week).
